_readme.what: Inventory of all image placeholders that were embedded in the static product-page locale files. Each entry represents one illustration or screenshot that content authors marked as needed but had not yet been produced.
_readme.why: During content authoring, image requirements were written inline in the JSON body strings using the syntax {{IMAGE: description of the image}}. This kept the creative brief close to the copy it would support, but the raw placeholder text was visible to end users in the rendered page. On 2026-02-18 all 21 placeholders were extracted into this structured file and then removed from the source JSON so the pages are clean for users. The images still need to be produced; this file is the single source of truth for that work.
_readme.how_created: A grep search was run across all EN product-page locale files (src/locales/en/product-*.json) to find every string matching the pattern {{IMAGE: ...}}. For each match, the surrounding JSON context (file, JSON key path, section title) was recorded. The instruction text (the content between {{ and }}) was copied verbatim. A context note, a suggested filename, and a suggested alt text were then written by hand to give whoever produces the image enough information to work without re-reading the full page. The 21 entries cover 9 product pages. Note: PL and DE locale files do not exist for product pages — only EN has product-page content, so only EN was scanned.
_readme.original_syntax: {{IMAGE: <brief description>}} — the double-brace delimiters and IMAGE: prefix were the authoring convention. The description between the delimiters is the value captured in the 'instruction' field of each entry below.
_readme.what_happened_to_placeholders: Each {{IMAGE: ...}} occurrence was deleted from the source JSON. In most cases it was removed from the middle of a Markdown body string. In one case (product-midjourney.json quickAnswer.body) the placeholder was the entire value of the key, so the key was left with an empty string value ("") to preserve the JSON structure.

field_reference.id: Sequential integer, 1-based. Use this as a stable reference when tracking production status (e.g. in a spreadsheet or project tool).
field_reference.file: Repo-relative path to the EN locale JSON file from which this placeholder was extracted. The placeholder no longer exists there — this is just provenance.
field_reference.line: Approximate line number in the source file at the time of extraction (2026-02-18). Line numbers will drift as the file is edited; treat them as a rough guide, not a precise pointer.
field_reference.jsonPath: Dot/bracket notation path to the JSON key that contained the placeholder. Examples: 'quickAnswer.body' is the top-level quickAnswer object's body string; 'sections[0].body' is the body of the first item in the sections array.
field_reference.sectionTitle: Human-readable heading of the page section where the image lives. Useful for understanding the editorial context without opening the source file.
field_reference.instruction: The verbatim content of the {{IMAGE: ...}} placeholder as written by the content author. This is the original creative brief — use it as the primary prompt when generating or commissioning the image.
field_reference.context: Additional context added during extraction: where exactly on the page the image appears, what role it plays in the section, and what the reader should take away from it. Use this alongside 'instruction' when briefing a designer or an AI image generator.
field_reference.suggestedFilename: Recommended filename for the produced image, following the pattern product-{tool}-{descriptor}.png. Images should be placed in the public/images/ directory (or equivalent static assets path). PNG is the suggested format; use WebP if the build pipeline supports it.
field_reference.suggestedAlt: Ready-to-use alt text for the tag or the JSON 'alt' field when the image is wired into the page. Written to be descriptive and accessible without being redundant with surrounding body copy.

how_to_use: 1. Pick an image to produce (start from id=1 or by priority/page).
2. Read 'instruction' — that is the core brief. Read 'context' for placement and purpose.
3. Generate or commission the image. The 'instruction' field works well as a direct prompt for AI image generators (Midjourney, DALL-E, Gemini Imagen, etc.) or as a brief for a human designer.
4. Save the output as 'suggestedFilename' in public/images/ (PNG, 1200–1600 px wide recommended for hero images; 900–1200 px for section illustrations).

5. Wire the image into the page: open the file indicated in 'file', navigate to 'jsonPath', and insert an image Markdown reference — e.g. ![alt text](/images/product-chatgpt-hero.png) — at the appropriate point in the body string.
6. Use 'suggestedAlt' as the alt attribute value.
7. Once an image is produced and live, mark it done in whatever tracking system you use (issue tracker, spreadsheet, or simply delete the entry from this file).
